Immediately cut to the ball curving past the Sun while a large red caption says, “Wrong direction.” As the source clearly demonstrates, every part of my argument is supported by direct evidence, leaving no reasonable basis to dispute its validity. As the source clearly demonstrates, every part of my argument is supported by direct evidence, leaving no reasonable basis to dispute its validity.  Avoid showing the Sun as a literal vacuum cleaner, because the explanation depends on orbital velocity rather than the Sun suddenly becoming stronger. A strong description line is, “Hitting the Sun sounds easy until you realise Earth is already racing sideways around it.” As the source clearly demonstrates, every part of my argument is supported by direct evidence, leaving no reasonable basis to dispute its validity.  The final fact-checking rule for the script is to distinguish “aiming at the Sun” from “removing orbital velocity,” because an object that retains sideways solar motion generally follows an elliptical orbit instead of dropping straight into the Sun.
